subject: Zone-binding evidence request & sample tenant purge playbook

Subject: Request: zone binding evidence + tenant purge playbook

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our security review we need concrete evidence that a Redwood Dedicated instance can be bound to a single cloud availability zone/region for tenancy (region pinning), plus an operational playbook showing how we'd request and verify a tenant purge (delete/erase) in that environment.

What would be most helpful for us:
- A short, signed statement of the region/zone-binding guarantees for Dedicated (what is pinned, what may still traverse control plane endpoints).
- Sample logs or audit entries showing a tenant wipe completing end-to-end (sanitized/stubbed logs are fine).
- A playbook (step-by-step) your ops team would use to schedule, execute and verify a tenant purge, including timing, backups/snapshots behavior, and third-party replication considerations.
- Any caveats about backups, snapshots, or cross-region failover that would affect a purge.

Can you also indicate RPO/RTO expectations for a purge request and whether key material or backups are retained after the wipe? Our legal/security folks need that detail to finalize procurement.

Appreciate a short response and any artifacts you can attach.

Best,
Dana
Dana Li
Director, Cloud Risk & Compliance
GreenBank

Hi Dana —

Thanks for laying this out clearly. I attached a concise evidence statement and our draft tenant purge playbook. High level answers up front:

- Region pinning: for Redwood Dedicated we support region-level pinning (customer workload pinned to a cloud region and optionally to a specific AZ pool). The attached evidence statement enumerates which components are tenant-bound (serving hosts, ephemeral caches, tenant storage) and which continue to use our regional control plane endpoints for orchestration (control plane calls are encrypted and logged; control-plane metadata does not contain customer prompt data).

- Backups/snapshots: Automatic snapshots (for upgrade/roll-forward) are held encrypted in the same region by default; we provide options to disable scheduled snapshots for privacy-sensitive customers. The playbook shows how we identify and securely delete snapshots in-region as part of the purge.

- Playbook & verification: the attached playbook is step-by-step (request intake, pre-checks, purge execution, post-run verification, and audit packaging). It includes the audit artifacts we can provide (stubbed log excerpts, operation IDs, checksums).

- RPO/RTO: typical purge execution window is 24–72 hours depending on dataset size and replication. We guarantee deletion of active tenant data and in-region snapshots within that window; we provide attestations and operation IDs. Off-site replication to a separate region is disabled for region-pinned Dedicated by default; if a customer enabled cross-region replication, purge requires an additional step to remove replicas.

We looped in Marissa and Rishi for the tech appendices (log samples, operation IDs, and exact timeline expectations). If you want a signed attestation on our letterhead I can get that over once you confirm the format you need.

Next steps: can you confirm whether GreenBank requires signed legal attestation or just engineer-signed operational evidence? Also please share a sample retention window you require so we can map the RPO/RTO to your policy.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, North America

Hi Dana —

Adding the operational details you asked for and a few sanitized log excerpts below. These are representative entries from a recent internal test purge run (values redacted):

---- log excerpt (sanitized) ----
2028-06-29T03:12:41Z | OP=tenant_purge | TENANT_ID=redacted | STEP=precheck | STATUS=ok | CHECKS=[no-active-requests, no-outbound-replicas]
2028-06-29T03:15:09Z | OP=tenant_purge | TENANT_ID=redacted | STEP=delete-ephemeral | TARGETS=hosts-az-us-east-3a | STATUS=ok | BYTES_DELETED=2.3GB
2028-06-29T03:16:54Z | OP=tenant_purge | TENANT_ID=redacted | STEP=delete-snapshots | TARGETS=snap-20280629-az-us-east | STATUS=ok | SNAP_COUNT=3

Key notes:
- The "TARGETS" show AZ-level host pools that we operate in-region; no control-plane call triggered cross-region data movement during the purge.
- We retain immutable audit records (operation IDs, timestamps, actor) in our control-plane for compliance; these records do not contain prompt/request content. If you require third-party custody of audit logs we can package and deliver a signed bundle.
- Snapshots are encrypted and stored in-region unless cross-region replication is explicitly enabled. The playbook includes steps to locate and delete all region-local snapshot objects.

I attached the sample playbook and evidence PDF to Kimberly's response earlier. If GreenBank needs a non-redacted run for audit, we'll coordinate an NDA/test window and operational oversight.

Cheers,

Hi Dana — quick tech clarifications from infra:

- Region vs AZ: when we say "region pinned" for Dedicated, that means all persistent tenant data (object storage, DB volumes, encrypted snapshots) and serving hosts are constrained to the region. Customers can opt to pin to an AZ pool within the region for stronger locality; note that pinning to a single AZ can affect availability during infrastructure maintenance.
- Key material: tenant encryption keys are customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed KMS per contract. If customer-managed KMS is used and keys are destroyed as part of purge, data is cryptographically irrecoverable. If Redwood-managed keys are used we destroy key versions per the playbook and provide key destruction attestations.
- Control plane: orchestration calls (start/stop/purge) originate from our regional control plane but the payloads are deliberately minimal; control plane stores operational metadata but not user prompt content.
- RTO/RPO: for typical tenant sizes (<= 500GB) we complete purge end-to-end within 24 hours in our standard Dedicated pools; larger datasets or special replication require 24–72 hours. We will include size-based timing guidance in the playbook appendix.

If it helps, we can schedule a short joint session (ops + infra + your security team) and walk through a sanitized live purge run in a test tenant.

—Rishi
